title: Three-point Fourier functions
statement: On the set $\{a,b,c\}$, define three real-valued functions indexed by $0,1,2$. The function at index $0$ is constantly $1$; at index $1$ its values on $(a,b,c)$ are $\bigl(\sqrt{2},-\sqrt{2}/2,-\sqrt{2}/2\bigr)$, and at index $2$ they are $\bigl(0,\sqrt{6}/2,-\sqrt{6}/2\bigr)$.
